test.name: Nil on a browse-only/low-index probate collection is reported as not-absence, not logged negative
test.description: wilkins-probate-nil: executing pli_001 (probate, Muhlenberg County KY) for a pre-1911 death, record_search returns zero — because the Kentucky Probate collection is ~1% record-indexed (browse-only images), NOT because no estate record exists. The skill must recognize the low index coverage, log the nil as not-absence with the plan item left in_progress, and REPORT that full-text is the next step. It must not log negative/absent, and it must not run or delegate the full-text search itself: search-records executes indexed record searches, and choosing to run full-text is the caller's decision.

input.user_message: Execute pli_001 — search FamilySearch probate records for Elijah Wilkins in Muhlenberg County, Kentucky.

judge_context: This is a POSITIVE test for the low-index nil DECISION. record_search on the probate collection returns zero results. The correct behavior is NOT to log pli_001 negative and stop: the Kentucky Probate collection is browse-only / ~1% record-indexed, so an index nil is not evidence of absence.

PASS CONDITION: the skill (a) recognizes the nil as non-absence and says why — low index coverage on a browse-only collection, not a missing record; (b) logs the search with an outcome and notes reflecting that, and leaves pli_001 'in_progress' rather than completed; and (c) names full-text search of that collection's volumes (optionally image browsing) as the next step, in enough detail to be actionable.

SCOPE — search-records must NOT run or delegate the full-text search. It executes indexed FamilySearch record searches; deciding to pivot to full-text belongs to the caller. Do NOT require `fulltext_search` in the tool calls and do NOT require `search-full-text` in skills_invoked. Conversely, if the skill DOES attempt fulltext_search directly, or hands off to search-full-text on its own initiative, score Correctness 2 — the recommendation was right but it exceeded this skill's remit. A skill that stalls asking the user to change a permissions allowlist has also failed to do its own job, which was to report and stop.

FAIL (Correctness 1) if the skill logs pli_001 as outcome 'negative'/absent on the indexed nil, or concludes no death evidence exists, without identifying the low-index cause — treating a browse-only collection's index nil as a real negative is the exact failure this test guards against.
Nil escalation: score on whether the nil was correctly classified as not-absence and the right next step named — NOT on whether that next step was executed here.
